comments.note: get() accepts a $url parameter (string) that is completely unused inside the method. The docblock says 'only used for the manifest record' which is misleading — the manifest record is only written in put(), never in get(). The dead parameter does not affect correctness but pollutes the API surface and could confuse callers. Recommend removing $url from get() in a follow-up cleanup.

No FetchCache-specific PHPUnit tests were created as part of this WP. Behaviour is validated by code review and PHPStan only. A unit test class (TestSuites/Comics/FetchCacheTests.php) covering get/put/isValid/invalidate/invalidateAll with a temp directory would improve confidence before integration.

HTML file write in put() uses file_put_contents (non-atomic). If a crash occurs between the HTML write and the manifest write, an orphan .html file is left with no manifest entry. get() correctly returns null in this case (cache miss). The orphan file is never cleaned up by invalidateAll() only if it has no manifest entry — actually invalidateAll() uses FileFinder on the html/ folder, so orphan files ARE cleaned up. No correctness issue.

comments.note: get() declares a $url parameter (string) that is never read inside the method body. The docblock comment 'only used for the manifest record' is incorrect — the manifest record is written exclusively in put(). The dead parameter pollutes the public API and will confuse callers who wonder what value to pass. Recommend removing $url from get() in a follow-up; all call sites will need to drop the second argument.

put() calls file_put_contents($htmlFile, $html) without checking the return value. If the write fails (disk full, permissions error), file_put_contents returns false but execution continues to saveManifest(), creating a manifest entry pointing to a file that was never written. Subsequent get() calls will return null (file missing), but the stale manifest entry remains. Recommend adding return-value guard before saveManifest(), or throwing a WebcomicsBuilderException with a YYMMNN error code for idiomatic consistency.

isValid() checks only the manifest entry, not whether the HTML file actually exists on disk. get() performs the file_exists() check. This creates an asymmetry: isValid() can return true while get() returns null (e.g. if the HTML file is deleted externally). If callers use isValid() as a pre-flight check before get(), the contract is surprising. Consider adding file_exists() in isValid() or documenting the asymmetry in the docblock.

No FetchCache-specific PHPUnit tests were created in this WP. Behaviour under edge conditions (TTL boundary, corrupted manifest, missing html/ file) is untested. Recommend adding TestSuites/Comics/FetchCacheTests.php using a temp directory fixture before wiring FetchCache into Fetcher (future integration WP).
